note_text:
Patient is a 58-year-old male with relapsed/refractory peripheral T-cell lymphoma who was started on pralatrexate therapy 4 weeks ago. He is tolerating treatment with mild mucositis. Review of labs prior to initiating pralatrexate showed serum B12 of 210 pg/mL (low-normal), and he was noted to have mild peripheral neuropathy attributed in part to subclinical B12 insufficiency. 

On chart review today, it is noted that the patient did not receive a vitamin B12 intramuscular supplementation injection prior to starting pralatrexate, nor has he received one since initiation four weeks ago. He is now due for his next cycle. Folic acid 1 mg daily has been continued per protocol, but the B12 component of the required supplementation regimen was inadvertently omitted at treatment start.

Plan: Administer vitamin B12 1 mg IM today, four weeks after starting pralatrexate, to correct the missed baseline dose, and re-establish the every 8-10 week dosing schedule going forward. Will document this deviation from protocol timing in the chart and monitor for signs of worsening neuropathy or hematologic toxicity in the interim.
